question.problem:
The probability mass function of the random variables $X$ and $Y$ are given below.
$x$ $0$ $1$ $2$ $3$
$f(x)$ $0.1$ $0.6$ $0.2$ $0.1$
$y$ $0$ $1$ $2$
$f(y)$ $0.5$ $0.3$ $0.2$

Find $\text{E}[3Y-X].$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if $X$ and $Y$ are random variables (not necessarily independent), and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then

$$
\text{E}[aX+bY]=a\text{E}[X]+b\text{E}[Y].
$$

First, let's find $\text{E}[X]$ and $\text{E}[Y].$ If $X$ is defined on a sample space ${S}_{x},$ then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{x\in {S}_{x}}x\cdot f(x) \\  & =0\cdot 0.1+1\cdot 0.6+2\cdot 0.2+3\cdot 0.1 \\  & =1.3.\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, if $Y$ is defined on a sample space ${S}_{y},$ then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={\sum }_{y\in {S}_{y}}y\cdot f(y) \\  & =0\cdot 0.5+1\cdot 0.3+2\cdot 0.2 \\  & =0.7.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[3Y-X] & =\text{E}[3Y]+\text{E}[-X] \\  & =3\text{E}[Y]-\text{E}[X] \\  & =3\cdot 0.7-1.3 \\  & =0.8.\end{aligned}
$$
